Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Planning Commission Members will be participating via

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city/agendas and available for
viewing thereafter. Commission meetings are recorded for minutes preparation purposes.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:

a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol Corea, Administrative  Assistant  at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”

you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting, may join by visiting http://www.zoom.com/join
and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 824 5396 4592 Passcode: 049036.

- If using a tablet or phone, download the Zoom app and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 824 5396
4592 Passcode: 049036

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  TUESDAY, JULY 6, 2021

  An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
  to order by CHAIR EDLER at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this
  meeting was held via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR EDLER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Carman, Edler, Medawar, Schachter, Scott, Yoo, Zigrang

  City Staff Present:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, JUNE 7, 2021

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSION YOO
  to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, JUNE 7,
  2021

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  APPROVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED
  FOR CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READY BY TITLE ONLY.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE ITEM NO. 6A

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210169; ADDRESS: 27063 PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  EAST; APPLICANT: CHRIS BENNETT, CHADMAR/COLFIN ROLLING HILLS, LLC.; A
  request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-210170) for a new two-story
  single-family residence.

  Planning Manager Naughton presented Planning Application No. PA-210169, a request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for a new two-story single-family residence on a vacant
  lot. Previously the site was used as overflow parking for the Rolling Hills Country Club and
  subsequently used by the Chandler Palos Verdes Sand and Gravel Company. In 2011, there were
  entitlements approved for a reconfiguration of the Rolling Hills Country Club golf course, a new
  club house, and a tract map to approve 114 single-family residences. 113 of the single-family lots
  were located within the former Chandler Palos Verdes Sand and Gravel Company area; the 114th
  single-family lot was located at the subject site, which is addressed 27063 Palos Verdes Drive
  East. In 2015 grading began for the project, and hundreds of trees both from the interior and
  perimeter of the site were removed. There was also a reduction of grades on the northern view
  corridor of the subject site, which opened new view corridors for properties to the south and
  southwest of the subject site.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, JULY 6, 2021
  1
   Prior to and after the entitlements were approved in 2011, the subject site and part of the golf
  course to the north were zoned RA-20. In 2011, the zoning for the north part of the golf course was
  changed to Commercial Recreation and the residential portion was changed to Residential
  Planned Development. The subject site remained zoned RA-20 with a horse overlay.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided an exhibit showing the location and the site of the home
  after the first silhouette was revised and moved back by 12.1 ft. The exhibit shows the horse
  keeping area in the western edge of the property and the house is setback from front property line
  by 89.1 ft. The RHE Municipal Code requires 25 ft. The proposal includes 3,900 sq. ft. on the first
  level and a three-car side facing garage, the second floor includes 1300 sq. ft. The proposed height
  is just under 27 ft.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that she received a call from the property owner of 27121
  Palos Verdes Drive East regarding view impairments. Staff went out to the site and took photos;
  photos comparing the views from the first and second site visits were included with the staff report.
  It was determined, at the first visit, that there were significant view impairments from the master
  bedroom looking towards the northerly view corridor, which included impacts to the LA Basin,
  Downtown LA and San Gabriel Mountains. Staff contacted the applicant, and they were amenable
  to shift the silhouette back to try to get out of the view corridor. A photo sent to Planning Manager
  Naughton via text by the property owner at 27121 Palos Verdes Drive North was provided; the
  photo was taken from her master bedroom where the property owner believes the silhouette is still
  impacting her view. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the difficulty with this site is that the
  lot has been vacant for a long time and any structure on this site is going to block some type of
  views. If the silhouette is shifted forward, it would block views from the master bedroom; if it is
  shifted further back, it would render an even greater portion of the lot unusable.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that in staff’s assessment, full resolution of view impacts would
  not likely be accomplished for either a one or two-story residence. The objective was to preserve
  the views from the master bedroom of the San Gabriel Mountains and Downtown LA and in staff’s
  opinion, shifting the silhouette back 12.1 ft. did accomplish that.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that since the subject site is not part of any HOA, staff looked
  at the closest residences to the site, in the DLPOA, and the homes on Casaba Road, for
  Neighborhood Statistics. This home would be larger than any other home by 33 sq. ft.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
  Planning Application No. PA-210169, a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for the
  construction of a new two-story single-family residence on a vacant lot, subject to the conditions
  outlined in the staff report.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT inquired about the neighbor’s master bedroom, which looks like it may have
  been a patio that was enclosed and asked if that was part of the square footage of the house.
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that it is not and confirmed that the home is actually larger
  than 4,300 sq. ft. and the enclosed area is approximately 260 sq. ft. VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated
  that previously there was mature landscaping that impacted this view corridor and stated that it
  would be good to see photos of what the view looked like prior to the project. Planning Manager
  Naughton stated that she asked the property owner for photos, but they were unable to locate any;
  in turn she looked at the Environmental Impact Report that was certified for the Chandler
  Ranch/Rolling Hills Country Club project, the pre-grading and post-grading elevations, the certified
  tree survey as part of the EIR, and historic google earth photos to get to the conservative 10 – 40
  ft. of grade reduction. VICE CHAIR SCOTT commented that he is not sure that the current view
  corridor is representative of the view corridor they had prior to the project.

  CHAIR EDLER opened the public comment period.

  Chuck Lande, The Chadmar Group, stated that prior to the project, there virtually were no views
  from the adjacent residence. Mr. Lande stated that when Planning Manager Naughton came to
  them with the neighbor’s view corridor issues, they volunteered to move the building back a little
  over 12 ft. and opened it up and still left good position of the home on the lot.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT commented on the photo of the second silhouette where there is a large
  Eucalyptus and stated that the ridge likely came after or approximately 100 ft. after that tree. Mr.
  Lande responded that he believes that is correct.

  Planning Manager Naughton presented a video provided by the architect with a video rendering of
  the proposed project.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked if the applicant provided an image of the materials that will be
  used. Planning Manager Naughton stated that the plans call out the materials but there was no
  image provided.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, JULY 6, 2021
  2
   Leah Robertson, 27121 Palos Verdes Drive East, stated that they have owned the home since
  1977 and stated that from the bedroom they had a view of the golf course and a partial city lights
  view and stated that she is concerned with the view corridor which is being blocked. She stated
  that it is too large and does not fit into the neighborhood. Ms. Robertson stated that the city is siding
  very heavily with the developer and stated that most cities are not pro-developer. She also stated
  that the City’s codes are not being followed and cannot believe that this is being considered since
  it is blocking views. She referenced a section of code that states, “determine whether other suitable
  design options are available” and stated that this has not been approached even though this was
  discussed in meetings with staff. She stated that there are a lot of people who are upset about the
  size of this project. Ms. Robertson requested that the meeting be deferred to be able to come to a
  mutual agreement with the applicant. She also asked for the Commissioners to visit the site. She
  also stated that Casaba should not be the homes to use for neighborhood statistics and it should
  be Montecillo and Dapplegray as a whole. Ms. Robertson stated that the lot still has 20,000 sq. ft.
  of usable space and can be moved back or it would be much more desirable as a one-story home.
  She also added that the views from the second floor have not improved as much as they should in
  her opinion.

  Mr. Linden Robertson, 27121 Palos Verdes Drive East, stated that the house was built in 1975 and
  stated that the house was situated in way to have views to the fairway and the long view corridor.
  Mr. Robertson stated that the proposed home is already covering 80% and asked if it could just be
  one-story and cover 100% instead of the intrusive second story, which he stated covers the back
  of the home and their backyard. He stated that when this project was originally set-up, everyone
  was supposed to get a view and have an improvement of their view. He stated that Casaba homes
  conform to the topography of the neighborhood and there are no other homes that are intrusive as
  this proposed home. Mr. Robertson stated that the single lot is not part of the RHCC development.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked Mr. Robertson if he was part of the sale of group that sold this project
  and stated that he had the ability to put a deed restriction on this lot. He stated that looking at the
  photos, they are good views. The views from the kitchen are blocked by the Robertson’s own
  landscaping by 90%. Mr. Robertson stated, “that lot wasn’t originally part of the project, that came
  in later. That lot was given to Rolling Hills Golf Course and then Chuck Lande got it away from
  them in some kind of deal.” VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that their views have already improved
  and building on the current flagged lot does not materially impair any valuable views. VICE CHAIR
  SCOTT stated that if a one-story home farther forward, will negatively impact their view corridor.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if there is any second story that could be acceptable on
  this lot. Ms. Robertson stated that she is amenable to other options. She stated that she knows
  that some views will be impacted and asked that they are able to work together with the applicant
  to come to a resolution.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that they have already given up a large portion of their front
  yard and stated that if the house would be 40 ft. forward, the property would be worth a lot more.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if restrictions could be imposed for planting trees in the
  front 75 – 80 ft. so that further views are not blocked. Planning Manager Naughton stated that these
  could be included in the conditions of approval and there is a process in the municipal code for
  view loss due to landscaping.

  Robert Haffey, Resident of Montecillo Neighborhood, stated that he has been a proponent of the
  RHCC project, but stated that he has walked by the proposed project and was struck by how
  massive the proposed project is and is concerned with what could happen if his neighbors propose
  to build a similar size home. Mr. Haffey stated that the house has been moved back but the second
  story is still in an area that impedes views. He also stated that the Casaba homes are different due
  to the topography and none appear massive although they have the square footage. He also stated
  that it looks different and intrusive of other homes in the City. He reiterated that he is concerned
  with similar projects being proposed by his neighbors.

  Jane Nicklas, Resident, stated that she has walked by this home and expressed her concern with
  the precedent this home is setting. Ms. Nicklas stated that she thinks this home will be a
  “McMansion” and the homes that this is being compared to are newer homes. She stated that she
  is concerned that neighbors are allowed to build similar homes and block her views. Ms. Nicklas
  expressed her concern with the home having to be two stories.

  Mr. Haffey inquired why the two balconies are facing toward the neighbor and not toward the view
  corridor.

  CHAIR EDLER closed the public comment period.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that it does not have to be a two-story house, but the lot is
  zoned for two stories. He also stated that they have done a good job of mitigating the size of the

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, JULY 6, 2021
  3
   second story with it being 1,300 sq. ft. If they wanted to put the second story towards the rear, it
  would help the dispute between the neighbors, but he is in favor of this project.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN asked for what are considered preserved views when related to
  developments. Planning Manager Naughton stated the RHEMC Chapter 17.54 addresses view
  protection but is general in its description of view corridors. In this case, it would be difficult to
  maintain all the existing views because the lot is vacant. She further explained how the views could
  be blocked depending on the location of the house on the lot. COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated
  that she empathizes with the Robertson’s, but also has had to lean with her colleagues regarding
  property rights and finding a balance. She stated that there have been enhancements to the views
  that have been impacted, but the commitment of the applicant to move the house back has gone
  a long way. COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that she would like to see a color rendering of the
  proposed residence and the design of the front façade since Palos Verdes Drive East is an
  important view corridor. She added that lowering the height may help for the Robertson’s view.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that he is assuming Palos Verdes Drive East coming up the hills is
  view corridor in the General Plan. He stated that setting the house so far back mitigates the large
  size. He stated that moving the second story to the rear may help marginally. VICE CHAIR SCOTT
  stated that the impacts to view corridors are minimal in his opinion. He stated that he does not
  agree that this home is overly massive and the mitigation for the size of this home are effective.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that the opposition to this project has to do with policy not
  code. The applicant has been sensitive to the mass and anytime you put a home on an empty lot,
  there will be impact to views. He stated that he is in support of the project and stated that the
  applicant has done a great job.

  CHAIR EDLER agreed.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER stated that he agrees and stated that the applicant has done as
  much as he can do under the circumstances.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if the home is one-story and shifted forward, would the impact be
  greater on views. COMMISSIONER CARMAN and VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that the impact
  would be greater. COMMISSIONER YOO asked if an ADU could be built in the rear of the home.
  Planning Manager Naughton confirmed that an ADU can be built.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210169, A REQUEST FOR A
  NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY DETERMINATION (NC-210170) FOR A NEW TWO-
  STORY SINGLE FAMILY RESIDENCE ON A VACANT LOT, WITH THE ADDITIONAL
  CONDITION THAT LANDSCAPING BEGINNING AT THE FORWARDMOST BUILDING
  LINE, MOVING IN AN EASTERLY DIRECTION TOWARD THE FRONT PROPERTY LINE,
  TO A POINT, AS DETERMINED BY THE DIRECTOR OF COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT/PUBLC WORKS, IS RESTRICTED IN HEIGHT TO A MAXIMUM OF 14-
  FEET, SO AS TO REASONABLY PROTECT THE VIEW CORRIDOR OF THE ADJACENT
  NEIGHBORS LOCATED AT 27121 PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST; BEYOND THAT
  POINT,  AS  DETERMINED  BY  THE  DIRECTOR  OF  COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT/PUBLIC WORKS, LANDSCAPING MAY EXCEED A MAXIMUM HEIGHT
  OF 14-FEET.

  AYES: EDLER, SCOTT, CARMAN, MEDAWAR, SCHACTHER, YOO, ZIGRANG
  NOES:
  ABSENT:
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
  Application No. PA-210169, a request Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-210170) for
  a new two-story single-family residence on a vacant lot at 27063 Palos Verdes Drive East. There
  is a 20-day appeal period where any member of the public may appeal this decision to the City
  Council.

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  NONE

  9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT requested an update on 9 Lantana. DIRECTOR WAHBA stated that they got
  clearance from the Environmental Division with respect to distance from methane and the next step
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
MINUTES, JULY 6, 2021
  4
   is Fire Department clearance.

  10.  MANAGER ITEMS

  Planning Manger Naughton stated that the August Planning Commission meeting may be in-person.

  11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS (BUDGET STUDY SESSION) - JUNE 8, 2021

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS - JUNE 8, 2021

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 11A AND 11B

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR EDLER adjourned the Planning Commission meeting at 8:42 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Rick Edler, Chair
